fact: Bun chosen over Node.js for runtime — monorepo with workspaces
recommendation: Use Bun APIs and bun.lock, not npm/yarn

fact: Hono chosen as HTTP framework for lightweight, edge-compatible backend
recommendation: Follow Hono patterns for new routes, avoid Express-style middleware

fact: Zustand for state management — all state keyed by session ID
recommendation: New state slices must be session-scoped, never global singletons

fact: Auto-pipeline experiments target SMALL-to-MEDIUM scope (≤ 1 user story, ≤ 10 files, ≤ 700 LOC)
recommendation: Validated on Phase 1.5 (account switcher, 600 LOC, 47 new tests, ~85 min wall-clock). Quality matched manual Phase 1 (control-tower pattern). For LARGER scope ('content factory', 'multi-account threads platform'), do NOT use one giant auto-loop — decompose into a MODULAR ROADMAP where each phase is its own auto-pipeline run with operator ship gate between. Confirmation bias risk grows nonlinearly with scope; small phases keep council-review findings actionable and observer/external-eye review tractable.

fact: Future direction: unify council-* (originals) and council-*-aura into one stack-detecting skill pack
recommendation: Currently two parallel skill packs co-exist at ~/.claude/skills/ — council-{plan,review,implement} (Python/aiogram/Postgres-targeted per SKILL.md, though references already drifted to Next.js/Prisma) and council-{plan,review,implement}-aura (Bun/Hono/TS/React/FS-JSON/NDJSON). Maintaining both indefinitely costs documentation drift and confuses slash-command discovery. Future direction: collapse to ONE skill pack with stack auto-detection (likely probe project root for bun.lockb vs pyproject.toml vs Gemfile, choose expert panel + Phase 0 commands + reference docs accordingly). Mechanism TBD — could be either (a) SKILL.md branches on detected stack and dispatches the matching panel, (b) per-stack subdirectories with a thin top-level dispatcher, or (c) externalised stack-config that the SKILL.md reads. Deprecate the duplicate first-sources once the unified version is validated on both Aura and a Python project. Not a v1 blocker — current parallel setup works correctly; this is structural cleanup for the medium term.
